title: Typed-output compatibility gate: simulation & regression harness for strict-json enforcement
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: build a focused simulation and regression harness that exercises the strict typed-output (strict-json) enforcement layer across streaming responses, interleaved tool/function calls, and SDK compatibility layers. The harness should produce deterministic scenarios we can run in CI to measure two vectors: (1) enforcement false positives (valid model output flagged) and false negatives (invalid output allowed), and (2) operational impact (latency, token overhead, fallback rate). Deliverables: a set of canonical scenarios, an automated runner that spins up the runtime shim + decoder gate, integration hooks into our GitHub actions, and a first 30-day regression run baseline with metrics and remediation tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run deterministically against a local runtime binary and mocked SDK for streaming and non-streaming modes

At least 20 canonical scenarios covering: full valid JSON streaming, partial-chunked JSON, interleaved toolcalls that inject non-JSON tokens, truncated-last-chunk cases, and KV-cache re-use across requests
CI job added that runs the harness on every merge to runtime and decoder components (non-blocking for now)
Baseline metrics recorded and uploaded to the dashboard: enforcement-fallback-rate, mean additional latency introduced, and false-positive percentage
Automatic creation of a remediation issue when fallback-rate > 0.5% for a run of 1,000 synthetic requests
test_plan: Scenario A: Streaming-valid - model returns well-formed JSON across 6 chunks; gate must allow and not trigger fallback
Scenario B: Streaming-partial - last chunk truncated mid-token; gate must attempt recovery and trigger fallback only if recovery fails
Scenario C: Interleaved-toolcall - tool return text injected between JSON fragments; gate must tolerate toolcall markers or use configured tool sentinel handling
Scenario D: Loose-compat - model occasionally emits single-word prefix before JSON object (legacy SDK clients); gate must have a compatibility whitelist mode and metric whether whitelist was used
Scenario E: KV-cache-replay - repeated requests reuse cache and produce identical prefixes; ensure enforcement does not degrade when cache re-inserts prompt fragments
Scenario F: Backpressure/drop - simulate network stalls dropping chunks; gate must not assert invalid JSON prematurely and must report partial-stream incidents
Load test: 1k synthetic streaming requests with distribution: 50% A, 20% B, 15% C, 10% D, 5% F to measure latency and fallback-rate
implementation_notes: We will implement the harness as a small Go binary that can run against either the local runtime binary or a dockerized test runtime. This mirrors existing integration approaches used by the ingest tests.

Decoder gate will be exercised via an instrumented runtime shim that emits event traces for: chunk-received, decode-decision(accept|fallback|recover), and fallback-reason. Trace IDs are correlated with synthetic request IDs.

Compatibility whitelist mode: implement a pluggable prefilter that can strip known legacy prefixes (e.g., 'Answer:' or single-token disclaimers) configurable per-test to compare strict vs tolerant behavior.
Tradeoff: strict enforcement reduces downstream parsing errors but may increase fallback rate and latency. The harness must capture these tradeoffs and produce tunable knobs for CI thresholds.
PRs and artifacts: initial prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124 (harness + shim), follow-up PR will add GitHub Action and dashboard uploader
Telemetry: metrics will be pushed to the test metrics endpoint under namespace 'typed_output_harness' with labels scenario, runtime_commit, and decoder_config
